disclaimer: Early reports, no IOCs yet. Not on the block list.

rumours.claim: German drone maker Quantum Systems confirmed a late-October cyberattack; reports say a malicious QBase update reached customer servers, and no public IOCs have been published.
rumours.note: The company says the incident was contained and there is no risk to operators. Der Spiegel and the Financial Times, cited by later reporting, describe a compromised QBase update server. Attribution is unconfirmed.
rumours.headline: German military drone maker hit by malicious software update

rumours.claim: Europol and partners seized 235 servers and 257 domains used by Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC, and identified 6.4 million stolen credentials; no public remaining-infrastructure block list has been published.
rumours.note: Victim notifications are being issued through Have I Been Pwned and partner channels. WordPress site owners are advised to rotate credentials and enable multi-factor authentication.
rumours.headline: Police seize Gootloader and StealC servers, recover 6.4 million credentials
Maersk confirms data theft from acquired logistics system as WhiteArmor demands $5m
rumours.claim: Maersk confirmed unauthorised access and data extraction from a legacy system inherited through an acquisition; WhiteArmor claims about 100GB from the former LF Logistics platform, and no public IOCs have been published.
rumours.note: Maersk says the incident is isolated to a local system with no sign of impact on other Maersk, customer or partner systems connected through APIs and EDI, and advises treating unexpected messages about the incident with caution. Maersk told Cybernews the plaintext-password claim is not accurate. Partners of the former LF Logistics platform should watch for phishing that references the incident.

rumours.claim: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 patches a critical unauthenticated HTTP/2 flaw in mod_http2 (CVE-2026-119618); no public in-the-wild exploit indicators have been published.
rumours.note: Affects Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 when HTTP/2 is enabled. Upgrade to 2.4.71, or remove h2 and h2c from Protocols until patched. This is a vendor-confirmed flaw, not a rumour of exploitation.
rumours.headline: Apache patches critical HTTP/2 flaw, no public exploit indicators yet

rumours.claim: A new extortion brand, PixelLeaks, appeared on a leak site in early November 2026 with claimed victims in several countries; the claims are not independently confirmed and no public IOCs have been published.
rumours.note: Trackers list first activity around 9 November 2026. Victim names come from the group's own leak site and should be treated as claims until a victim or a reputable investigation confirms them. No leak-site links are published here.
rumours.headline: New PixelLeaks extortion brand claims victims in several countries
